merger_name: EQT Fund Management S.à r.l. – Orikan Group

anzsic_codes.name: Computer System Design and Related Services

merger_description:
Ulexite Group Pty Limited, an indirectly wholly owned special purpose vehicle of BPEA EQT Mid-Market Growth Fund (**BPEA MMG**), proposes to acquire 100% of the issued capital of Ignition TopCo Pty Ltd (**Ignition**), together with its subsidiaries (together, the **Orikan Group**), pursuant to a share sale agreement (the **Acquisition**).

BPEA MMG is a private investment fund controlled by EQT Fund Management S.à r.l. (**EFMS**), its alternative investment fund manager. EFMS is wholly owned by EQT AB (publ) (Sweden).

Ignition is the ultimate holding company in the Orikan Group. The Orikan Group is a provider of parking management, compliance, and mobility technology solutions and associated services. Its products support parking payments, digital permits, parking enforcement, infringement management, occupancy monitoring, reporting, and customer service functions mainly for local governments, universities, hospitals, airports and transport authorities. The Orikan Group also provides implementation, support, maintenance, and outsourced operational services related to these systems.

determination_table_content.details:
Ulexite Group Pty Limited (Ulexite) applied for a notification waiver in
respect of its proposed acquisition of 100% of the issued share
capital in Ignition TopCo Pty Ltd (together with its subsidiaries,
Orikan Group), as described in the transaction documents provided
as part of the application (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The acquirer, Ulexite, is an indirectly wholly owned subsidiary of
BPEA EQT Mid-Market Growth Fund (BPEA MMG). BPEA MMG is a
private investment fund controlled by EQT Fund Management S.à r.l.,
an alternative investment fund manager. EQT Fund Management
S.à r.l. is wholly owned by EQT AB (publ) (Sweden).
The target, Orikan Group, is a provider of parking management,
compliance, and mobility technology solutions and associated
services. Its products support parking payments, digital permits,
parking enforcement, infringement management, occupancy
monitoring, reporting, and customer service functions mainly for
local governments, universities, hospitals, airports and transport
authorities. The Orikan Group also provides implementation, support,
maintenance, and outsourced operational services related to these
systems.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. There is no horizontal or vertical overlap in Australia
between the acquirer (or its connected entities) and Orikan Group (or
its connected entities), including in the supply of parking
management, compliance, and mobility technology solutions and
associated services.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
